title: NFTMinterV2.mintFor() ignores the paused flag, allowing authorized minters to keep minting during a global pause
description: NFTMinterV2 has its own internal `paused` flag set by the Global Pauser (L111-L122). The paid mint path `_executeMint` enforces `require(!paused, "Contract is paused")` on L171. However, `mintFor(uint256 index, address recipient)` has no `!paused` check. mintFor is the entry point used by NFTMigrator and other 'authorized minters' to issue claim NFTs without payment or dispatch. Because mintFor bypasses the paused flag entirely, an authorized minter (NFTMigrator, or any operational address with authorizedMinters[addr] == true) can continue issuing NFTs while the global pause is engaged. Combined with the fact that those freshly minted NFTs become immediately transferable (ERC1155 transfers are not pause-gated either), this means a Global Pause does not actually freeze new claim supply.
exploit_path:
1. Global Pauser detects incident and calls NFTMinterV2.pause(). The `paused` flag is true.
2. An authorized minter (e.g., a misconfigured operational bot, a compromised authorized address, or the live NFTMigrator with users still calling migrate()) calls mintFor(index, recipient). The call succeeds because there is no pause check.
3. New claim NFTs continue to enter circulation while the rest of the protocol is supposed to be frozen. The downstream burn/claim paths that consume these NFTs may also be unsafe in the paused state, and the operator cannot stop supply growth without either revoking the authorized minter (setAuthorizedMinter) or pausing every dispatcher individually.

The expected operator mental model — 'pause stops minting' — is violated. ClaimMintedFor events fire as if nothing is wrong.
mainnet_realism_check: This is a pure code-level invariant, no AMM dependency. The paused flag exists, paid mints honour it, mintFor does not. NFTMigrator on mainnet would be a registered authorized minter (per the deployment plan in the migration story), and any user calling NFTMigrator.migrate() would silently bypass the global pause. No mock assumption is required.
recommendation: Add `require(!paused, "Contract is paused")` to mintFor (and audit burn() for the same property — the current burn() also ignores paused; the team should decide whether burning during pause is intentional). At minimum, mintFor should be paused-gated because it issues new claims with no payment guard.
severity_rationale: Downgraded from initial Medium guess to Low/QA. The `paused` flag in NFTMinterV2 gates `_executeMint` (paid path) but not `mintFor` (authorized-minter path used by NFTMigrator). This is a real coverage gap: an operator engaging the Global Pause expects new claim supply to halt, but authorized minters can continue. However: (1) mintFor is restricted to authorizedMinters (an owner-controlled allow-list), so external attackers cannot trigger it; (2) it may be by design — migration via NFTMigrator should arguably continue through an unrelated incident pause on the paid mint path; (3) burn() also ignores paused, suggesting the pause may be scoped specifically to the paid economic flow rather than all NFT issuance. No documentation explicitly justifies the asymmetry, so this is a spec/state-handling clarification rather than a direct vulnerability. Per C4 QA/Low: 'State handling, function incorrect as to spec' — fits Low. Team should explicitly document the pause scope and decide whether mintFor/burn should honour it.
